editorial:
Imagine starting a new job thinking you can change the world, only to find out the world changes you instead. You follow a young guy who joins the LAPD just to pay for law school. He is bright-eyed and wants to do things by the book, but he quickly gets paired with a grumpy, old-school partner who doesn't care about rules. The movie feels like a slow burn that shows you how the grit and stress of the street can eat away at a person. It is not your typical flashy cop show; it is more about the mental toll of the job and how it pulls you away from the people you love.

The acting is top-notch and makes the relationship between the two partners feel real. While the pace is a bit slow at times, the tension builds up in a way that keeps you interested. You will love how it avoids cheesy tropes, though some might find the ending a bit sad. If you want to see it, try renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best picture quality. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend when you want something with actual depth.
endingExplained: By the end, you see the rookie has completely changed. He is no longer the sweet student he used to be. He has become cold and cynical, just like his partner. He loses his family and his dreams of becoming a lawyer because the police life took over everything. The movie wraps up by showing that the system won. He didn't fix the police force; instead, the force broke him down until he fit right in.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves realistic character studies and old school crime dramas.
